items.title: ATF prices increased by around ₹16 per litre; commercial LPG rises ₹62.50
items.summary:
Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices were raised by a steep Rs 16 per litre from Thursday, while the price of commercial LPG was increased by Rs 62.50 per 19-kg cylinder in step with firming international benchmarks, according to state-owned oil companies.
ATF prices were increased to Rs 137 per litre from Rs 121 for domestic airlines, according to the oil companies.
The latest revision comes after ATF prices were raised by Rs 6.28 per litre, or 5.46 per cent, in September, following a Rs 5 per litre increase in August. ATF accounts for up to 40 per cent of operating costs for airlines, making fuel prices a key cost factor for carriers.
Alongside, commercial LPG rates were hiked by Rs 62.59 per 19-kg cylinder.

items.title: Check top 10 richest Indians and full list
items.summary: Gautam Adani has reclaimed the No. 1 spot on the 2026 Forbes list of India's 100 richest, ending a three-year run as the country's second-richest person. A $20.7 billion jump took the Adani family fortune to $112.7 billion.According to the list released by Forbes on Thursday, the combined wealth of the 100 richest Indians is unchanged at about $1 trillion from the last time fortunes were measured. This comes in a year when the rupee fell 8.5 per cent and the stock market dropped 9.5 per cent.Also read: Gautam Adani reclaims top spot as India’s richest, edges out Mukesh Ambani: Hurun Rich ListAdani is the biggest gainer in dollar terms. His family wealth is still below the $150 billion peak it hit in 2022. The Adani Group is on an expansion drive and is investing $100 billion in AI infrastructure.Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani moves to No. 2 with a net worth of $86.3 billion. That is a fall of $18.7 billion. Margin pressures, including in retail, weighed on Reliance shares.Ambani is preparing for the listing of Jio Platforms. The telecom arm has received regulatory approval for an IPO that could raise up to $3.8 billion. That could make it the country's largest public offering to date.Savitri Jindal of the O.P. Jindal Group stays at No. 3 and remains India's richest woman. Her fortune edges down to $39.8 billion.Steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal jumps eight places to No. 4. His net worth rises 74 per cent to $34.7 billion. In May, he and Adar Poonawalla, son of No. 6 Cyrus Poonawalla, bought the IPL team Rajasthan Royals in a deal that valued the franchise at $1.65 billion.The fortunes of more than half the listees fell. AI-led automation has hurt India's software services sector, and tech billionaires felt the impact. Shiv Nadar (No. 7, $27.4 billion), Azim Premji (No. 32, $7.87 billion) and N.R. Narayana Murthy (No. 78, $3.95 billion) all saw their wealth decline.Infosys co-founders Nandan Nilekani and Senapathy Gopalakrishnan are among 11 people who dropped off the list.Separately, the M3M Hurun India Rich List 2026 also put Adani at the top, with his family's wealth rising 13 per cent to Rs 9.23 lakh crore ($96 billion), ahead of Ambani and family at Rs 8.63 lakh crore ($90 billion), a fall of 10 per cent.The Hurun list, which covers 1,810 individuals with wealth of at least Rs 1,000 crore, shows their combined wealth at Rs 187.5 lakh crore ($1.96 trillion), up 12.8 per cent from last year and equal to nearly half of India's GDP. India now has a record 391 dollar billionaires, up from 237 five years ago.The net worth figures differ from the Forbes list because the two rankings use different methodologies and valuation dates.Newcomers and returneesThere are four new entrants:Krishna Chivukula (No. 66, $4.35 billion), whose precision engineering firm Indo-MIM listed in JulyKushal and Chaitanya Desai (No. 69, $4.25 billion), after shares of their cables company Apar Industries nearly doubledAditya Khemka (No. 83, $3.6 billion), whose security equipment maker Aditya Infotech went public in 2025The Virani brothers (No. 90, $3.45 billion), behind Balaji Wafers, which sold a minority stake to US private equity firm General Atlantic in JanuarySeven people returned to the list. They include Anil Agarwal (No. 41, $6.4 billion), who split Vedanta into five listed entities in June. The minimum net worth to make the list fell to $3 billion from $3.2 billion last year.Top 10 richest Indians, 2026Gautam Adani and family: $112.7 billionMukesh Ambani: $86.3 billionSavitri Jindal: $39.8 billionLakshmi Mittal: $34.7 billionSunil Mittal and family: $32.9 billionCyrus Poonawalla: $28.4 billionShiv Nadar: $27.4 billionDilip Shanghvi: $26.3 billionKumar Birla: $23.2 billionHinduja family: $21.2 billionForbes used shareholding and financial data from families and individuals, stock exchanges, analysts and regulators. Unlike its world billionaires ranking, this list includes family fortunes shared among extended families, such as the Bajaj and Burman families.Also read: Ambani uses ₹10 power again for the next disruption in a hot Indian marketNet worths are based on stock prices and exchange rates at market close on September 11, 2026. Private companies are valued against similar listed firms.

items.title: Swiss glaciers lose 5.5% of ice volume in 2026, second-highest on record
items.summary:
Glaciers in Switzerland  the home to the most in the Alps  lost 5.5 per cent of their ice volume this year, the second-biggest percentage drop on record due to heat waves and low winter snowfall, experts report.
"Alpine glaciers have no chance of surviving in the long term under such conditions," the GLAMOS Swiss glacier monitoring service and Swiss Academy of Sciences said in a statement released Thursday.
The trend has worsened in recent years: Over the past five years alone, the volume of ice in Switzerland has declined by nearly a fifth, the experts say.
The report testifies to the latest concerns that global warming is wreaking havoc on Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent.
"The warming that we are experiencing now can be attributed 100 per cent to anthropogenic climate change. It's as simple as that," said Matthias Huss, who heads GLAMOS. "Without human emissions or fossil fuels, we wouldn't have any warming at the moment."

items.title: US economy grew 2.2% in Q2 on rising consumer spending, investment: US govt
items.summary:
The US economy grew at a solid 2.2 per cent pace from April through June as consumer spending and business investment came in strong.
Growth in gross domestic product - the nation's output of goods and services - decelerated from a 2.5 per cent pace from January through March, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. The second-quarter growth was an improvement on the department's previous estimate of 1.5 per cent - a surprise to economists who had expected little or no change in the GDP number.
Consumer spending - which accounts for about 70 per cent of US economic activity - increased at a healthy 3.8 per cent annual pace, up from 0.7 per cent in the January-March period. Spending has been helped by a strong stock market, which reflects enthusiasm over the prospects for artificial intelligence, enriches wealthy investors and gives them more money to buy things with.

items.title: US judge approves settlement, clearing $81 bn Paramount-Warner Bros. merger
items.summary:
A federal judge has now granted Paramount's settlement agreement with 12 states that sued over the company's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, allowing the companies to soon close their USD 81 billion mega merger.
In a Wednesday order, US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin ruled that the proposed consent decree was a "fair, reasonable, and good faith approach to address the competitive harms" alleged by the states' lawsuit. Paramount previously called the antitrust challenge the last hurdle ahead of closing its Warner merger, and signalled that it aims to close its Warner acquisition as early as October.
Shortly after Martinez-Olguin's ruling on Wednesday afternoon, the company announced that Ynon Kreiz - current chief executive at toy giant Mattel - will join Paramount on October 5 and serve as co-CEO alongside David Ellison of the combined company.
A Paramount-Warner marriage will bring together two of Hollywood's last five legacy studios. HBO Max, a library full of titles .

items.title: 'Captain Smit Machchhar is a hero': PM Modi

In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," PM Modi said in a post on X.His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy, he added.Also read: Former SpiceJet pilot at centre of Flydubai mid-air incidentThe prime minister further added that the country is proud of Captain Machchhar and is praying for his speedy recovery, renewed strength and good health.Dubai to Tel Aviv flight FZ1073 was flying with around 174 passengers when an incident involving the two pilots unfolded more than two hours into the flight. The aircraft then transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent before diverting to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia.Smit Machchhar health updateIndian Embassy in Saudi Arabia is following the health condition of Smit Machchhar, "the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk today."The Embassy informed that the pilot has admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and receiving necessary medical attention."A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition. We hope that he recovers from his injuries at the earliest. We are in touch with his family and assure them that we will continue to follow up on his health with Saudi authorities and extend all possible assistance for his wellbeing," it said in a statement.Also read: "Terrorist or whack job": Trump on flydubai co-pilot after mid-air attack; calls Indian Captain Smit Machchhar a heroNetanyahu hails pilot after stabbing issueIsraeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also hailed pilot Smit Machchhar for saving passengers after he was stabbed by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai plane.Passengers on the flight reached Israel safely after customers and crew foiled the co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said, as quoted by Reuters. The move allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot and enable a second pair of flydubai pilots who were on board to land the jet in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia."He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," Netanyahu said in a post on X. items.summary: Mumbai: Vijay Singh, vice chairman of Tata Trusts and a trustee of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), has approached the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner seeking an immediate inquiry into the administration and governance of the charitable trust, including its involvement in the commercial and strategic affairs of Tata Sons."I have written to the charity commissioner around the same time as Venu Srinivasan, expressing similar concerns," Singh told ET.Also read: ET Exclusive: Venu Srinivasan seeks probe into Tata Trusts over alleged governance lapsesAs reported first by ET on September 30, Srinivasan, Tata Trusts vice chairman and its joint nominee director on the Tata Sons board, has sought an inquiry into the appointment and continued status of Noel Tata as a perpetual trustee and the basis on which he assumed and continues to hold the chairmanship of Tata Trusts. He has also sought scrutiny of the appointment of son Neville Tata as a trustee.Call for Action Singh also demanded inquiry into what he described as his (Srinivasan's) exclusion from relevant decision-making processes.Singh's submissions are on similar lines, including seeking an examination of the involvement of SDTT and its trustees in the commercial and strategic affairs of Tata Sons.He has raised concerns over the increasing involvement of SDTT and Tata Trusts in matters concerning Tata Sons."SDTT's substantial shareholding in Tata Sons cannot mean that the trust assumes the functions of a commercial enterprise or participates directly in Tata Sons' business affairs," Singh said in the letter to the charity commissioner.Singh also flagged potential tax implications arising from such involvement, citing provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025, governing commercial activities by registered non-profit organisations. He has argued that activities not incidental to the trust's charitable objects could put its tax registration and exemption at risk."Given the substantial value of SDTT's shareholding in Tata Sons, the potential consequences for the trust and its charitable corpus could be immense," he has said.Also read: Tata companies face a tough call on Chandra vote at AGMThe two submissions - by Srinivasan and Singh - are now before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner. On Wednesday, Tata Trusts made a submission to the charity commissioner asking to be heard before the official takes any decision on the complaints.Singh has sought consequential action based on the findings of the inquiry, including suspension or removal of trustees where warranted and appointment of trustees in accordance with the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act.He has also sought directions under Section 36A(1) of the Act restraining SDTT and its board from convening meetings, passing circular resolutions or undertaking processes relating to the administration, management or composition of the trust until completion of the inspector's inquiry. Singh has asked that pending an inquiry, status quo be maintained in relation to the composition of the SDTT board of trustees.His move comes amid widening differences within Tata Trusts over the functioning of SDTT and the role of its trustees in matters concerning Tata Sons.The development also comes against the backdrop of proceedings concerning SRTT. In May, Maharashtra Charity Commissioner Amogh S Kaloti directed SRTT's board to postpone its May 16 meeting and refrain from convening such meetings until the submission of an inspector's report, following complaints concerning the composition of the board and alleged non-compliance with Section 30A(2) of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act.
